matched: Significance of study: mechanism-informed fouling prediction in data-limited plants via transfer learning from data-richer source plants
Pretrained LSTM model achieves reliable prediction in data-limited target plant, eliminating need to build prediction systems from scratch
Indicator selection framework: identify dominant fouling processes first, followed by extraction of representative fouling fingerprints
EPSc and EPSp contain transferable fouling information across MBR plants
Practical limitations of EPSc and EPSp: expensive, labor-intensive, difficult to monitor routinely
Feasible alternative: monitorable surrogate fingerprints such as online UV-vis and fluorescence spectral signals for plant-adaptive prediction and proactive fouling control [57]
Limitation: models developed from a limited number of pilot-scale MBRs with relatively similar operational backgrounds
Full-scale membrane fouling shaped by scale-dependent hydrodynamics, aeration, and greater operational variability [58], so pretrained relationships may not directly capture full-scale dynamics
Systems with different influent or operating conditions change sludge and EPS/SMP composition and dominant foulants, weakening transferable EPS signal and requiring plant-specific indicators
Framework requires validation on larger datasets and extension to full-scale, geographically diverse plants for robustness and generalizability
Prediction accuracy did not approach unity, indicating current indicator set remains incomplete
Target plant showed evidence of inorganic contributions, particularly iron-associated fouling revealed by CIP results, not fully captured by current model inputs

Identifying comprehensive indicators capturing combined organic and inorganic foulant effects supports earlier warning, better cleaning timing, reduced energy/chemical use, and process stability (Fig. S13)
